correctness.rationale: For each support edge (i,j), an open-neighborhood center (a,b) selects the XOR of row and column incidences, equivalently δ_F({r_a,c_b}); overlap at (a,b) cancels. Enumerating the three edge-shapes of size two and four relevant size-three types gives the stated binomial support coefficients and sharp m,n boundary conditions, including (m,n)=(1,1),(2,2),(2,4). A connected 3-edge path and 3-edge matching cannot yield the full trace; all qualified star/2-star-plus-edge shapes have explicit eight trace witnesses. The universal no-four-points step uses Adler–Benediktsson–Macpherson Theorem 4.6 VC≤3 for open neighborhoods of Hamming graphs and the induced-subgraph trace embedding, not finite enumerations. Independent direct trace enumeration on fifteen small boards (27,810 supports) agrees; finite checks do not prove the all-order bound.
residual_risks: All-order exclusion invokes an external published theorem; it was checked for open rather than closed neighborhoods.

value.rationale: A natural, complete labeled-support shattering polynomial for open neighborhoods on all complete rectangular rook graphs, beyond a scalar VC dimension. Sharp smallest 2×4 third-layer boundary and edge-shape classification distinguish boards with equal VC dimension; these data are plausible input to combinatorial learning/trace enumeration.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration and known VC bound alone would not establish value without the new coefficientwise structural formula.

limitations: Only complete rectangular rook graphs and open neighborhoods, not arbitrary induced Hamming graphs or closed balls; historical priority for mixed-alphabet shattering remains uncertain.
